title: resistor
description: Resistor component data. The presence of the 'resistor' field at the top level of an RAS document discriminates the device type — there is no deviceType property.

substitutesInfo.description: Replacement parts for this one: manufacturer-named successors and second sources. An entry with type 'successor' means THIS part is superseded by the named one, one hop, as the manufacturer states it - never inferred from a status of obsolete or from part-number similarity. The schema cannot check that the named part exists in the catalogue, or exists exactly once; that is the referential pass's job, as for CIAS component URIs. Evidence for the claim goes in the record's provenance[] with fields: ["substitutesInfo"], carrying the same sourceUrl, retrievedDate and verification stamp as any datasheet field.

anyOf.description: A sourced part: carries its manufacturer + datasheet.
A pre-sourcing seed: an empty resistor object whose requirements live in the enclosing PEAS document's inputs.designRequirements (mirrors CAS/SAS seed-friendliness).

technology.title: resistorTechnology
technology.description: Resistive-element construction of a fixed resistor. Referenced by part.technology and by the design-requirements side (inputs/designRequirements allowedTechnologies), so the two cannot drift. The per-value meanings are tabulated in docs/schema.md.

datasheetInfo.title: resistorDatasheetInfo
datasheetInfo.description: All information extracted from the resistor datasheet.

elements.description: One entry per resistor element in a network / array whose elements DIFFER (different resistance, tolerance or power rating per element, e.g. a divider or terminator network). Present INSTEAD OF the package-level electrical block, never beside it: such a network has no single resistance, and leaving a package-level slot open is what lets one element's numbers be recorded as the part's. A network of identical elements does NOT use elements[]: it keeps the one electrical block and states electrical.numberOfElements. The count is the length of elements[]. Order carries no meaning; elements are identified by name. (The RAS counterpart of SAS dies[].)

allOf.$comment: An internal connection relates elements: only a network (a count of identical elements, or elements[]) can state one.

element.title: resistorElement
element.description: One resistor element inside a network / array whose elements differ, with the complete electrical block the discrete file already defines — the same physics and the same field names as a discrete resistor, stated once per element. Every element states its own values even when the datasheet prints them as equal ('R1 = R2'), so 'both elements are 10 kOhm' and 'the part is 10 kOhm' are different documents.

name.description: The datasheet's own label for this element — 'R1', 'R2'. Unique within the part. Taken verbatim and never invented: a datasheet that does not distinguish its elements gives no element entries to write.

role.description: The datasheet's functional name for the element where it gives one ('pull-up', 'termination'), verbatim. Free text because vendors do not share a vocabulary; it is a label, never a substitute for the electrical data.

pins.description: Pin identifiers belonging to this element, matching entries of mechanical.pinout, so a circuit can bind to one element rather than to the package. A pin shared by several elements (the common terminal of a bussed network) is listed in the pins of EACH element it belongs to, consistent with part.internalConnection. The schema cannot check that the pinout contains these ids or that names are unique — that is the ingest gate's job.

electrical.description: The complete electrical block, per element. numberOfElements is not legal here: one entry is one element.

thermal.description: Per-element thermal figures where the datasheet gives them. The package-level figure stays in datasheetInfo.thermal.

internalConnection.description: How the elements of a resistor network / array are wired to each other INSIDE the package, when the datasheet says so. 'isolated' = no internal connection, each element has its own two terminals (Panasonic 'Isolated Circuit', Bourns 'Isolated'); 'bussed' = one end of every element is tied to a common terminal (Panasonic 'Common Terminal Circuit', Bourns 'Bussed'); 'centerCommon' = every element tied to a common terminal at the centre of the package (Panasonic 'Center Common'); 'diagonalCommon' = elements tied to a common terminal at a diagonal corner pin (Panasonic 'Diagonal Common, Pin1' / 'Pin5'; which pin goes in mechanical.pinout). Omit when the datasheet does not state it, or when its circuit is none of these (e.g. dual-terminator networks): describe those through mechanical.pinout — do not infer the arrangement from the package or the part number. Only legal on a network (electrical.numberOfElements or elements[]).

electrical.title: resistorElectrical
electrical.description: Resistor electrical characteristics. For a network / array of identical elements (electrical.numberOfElements), every value here is PER ELEMENT, never the package total.

numberOfElements.description: Number of IDENTICAL resistor elements in a network / array that this one electrical block describes (Panasonic 'Number of Elements'); every other value in the block is per element — resistance, tolerance and powerRating are the per-element figures the datasheet prints, never a package total (a package-level power rating, where printed, is not this field). A discrete resistor omits it. A network whose elements differ has no electrical block and no count field: it is described in datasheetInfo.elements[], whose length is the count.

temperatureCoefficient.description: Temperature coefficient of resistance, in ppm/K.

powerRating.description: Maximum power rating at the reference temperature, in W.

powerRatingTemperature.description: Reference temperature for the power rating, in Celsius.

maxVoltage.description: Maximum continuous working voltage, in V.

maxOverloadVoltage.description: Maximum short-pulse / overload voltage, in V.

factors.title: resistorFactors
factors.description: Derating factors as functions of temperature.
